numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With method="qr" the unpivoted QR factorization leaves R's diagonal in column order rather than decreasing magnitude, so the count of diagonal elements above tol depends on the column order of m; the same three columns with one a multiple of another return rank 3 in one order and rank 2 in the other five. The tolerance is also keyed to the first diagonal element rather than the largest. Downstream, DiscreteModel.initialize gets a df_model one too large and df_resid one too small for a rank-deficient design, shifting aic, bic and the model likelihood ratio test p-value on an unchanged likelihood.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The rank of a matrix is a property of its column space and must not depend on column order; the rank should be the same across all permutations of the columns. The QR factorization should be column pivoted (scipy.linalg.qr with pivoting=True) so that the diagonal of R is ordered by decreasing magnitude and tol is keyed to the largest diagonal element.
trigger_conditions: column order of m varies, e.g. the same columns permuted
a rank-deficient matrix where one column is an exact multiple of another
exog with an intercept and a regressor on a much larger scale (PR example)
caller DiscreteModel.initialize on a rank-deficient design

input_output_examples.input: three-column matrix m with one column an exact multiple of another, columns in one order (all six permutations tested)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: rank 3 in one column order, rank 2 in the other five
input_output_examples.expected_output: the same rank (2) for every column permutation

oracle_clues: A test asserts the same rank across all six permutations of a three-column exog under each of the three methods, and fails on qr without the fix (PR#10106 body)
Docstring of matrix_rank states the rank is the number of leading-diagonal elements of R above tol in absolute value
Existing test suites reported passing: statsmodels/tools/tests/test_tools.py 35 passed; discrete 1104 passed

numerical_characteristics.precision: The tolerance default is abs_diag[0] * m.shape[1] * np.finfo(float).eps, i.e. float64 machine epsilon scaled by column count; the test uses float values (1e3 * np.arange(1.0, 41.0) / 7.0, np.ones(40), 2.0 * x).
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Regressor x is on the order of 1e3 (values 1e3*k/7 for k=1..40) while the intercept column is ones, a much larger scale difference as described in the test comment.
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: Default tol = abs_diag[0] * m.shape[1] * np.finfo(float).eps when tol is None; the bug was that this was keyed to the first diagonal element rather than the largest.
category_specific_evidence: Property violated: rank is a property of the column space and must not depend on column order; the unpivoted QR count of diagonal entries above tol changes with column permutation.
Commit example: the same three columns, one a multiple of another, give rank 3 in one order and rank 2 in the other five orders.
Test test_matrix_rank_column_order asserts rank 2 for all permutations of exog = [ones, x, 2x] under methods ip, qr, svd; the qr case fails without pivoting.
Downstream effect: DiscreteModel.initialize gives df_model one too large and df_resid one too small, shifting aic, bic and the model likelihood ratio test p-value on an unchanged likelihood.
Fix: scipy.linalg.qr(m, mode="r", pivoting=True) orders the diagonal of R by decreasing magnitude so the existing tolerance is the intended one.
reproduction_risks: The exact ill-conditioning threshold depends on the default tolerance formula; reproduction should use the same tol default and column ordering to see the rank change.

The rank-3 versus rank-2 example in the commit message is given without the explicit matrix values, so the concrete reproducing matrix must be taken from the test (exog with ones, x, 2x) rather than assumed.
Passages do not state a dtype explicitly beyond float64 implied by np.finfo(float) and the float literals.

The rank of a matrix is a property of its column space and must not depend on column order; the rank should be the same across all permutations of the columns. The QR factorization should be column pivoted (scipy.linalg.qr with pivoting=True) so that the diagonal of R is ordered by decreasing magnitude and tol is keyed to the largest diagonal element.

The tolerance default is abs_diag[0] * m.shape[1] * np.finfo(float).eps, i.e. float64 machine epsilon scaled by column count; the test uses float values (1e3 * np.arange(1.0, 41.0) / 7.0, np.ones(40), 2.0 * x).
Regressor x is on the order of 1e3 (values 1e3*k/7 for k=1..40) while the intercept column is ones, a much larger scale difference as described in the test comment.
Default tol = abs_diag[0] * m.shape[1] * np.finfo(float).eps when tol is None; the bug was that this was keyed to the first diagonal element rather than the largest.
